correctness.rationale: The exact claim is proved for all m>=2, all positive conductances and all T>0. The spectral proof establishes simple spectrum and positive Gramian kernel for distinct weights, computes the characteristic polynomial at each edge conductance and obtains the precise ratios. The Krylov Vandermonde determinant is polynomial and extends to repeated weights, giving a necessary-and-sufficient single-sensor observability test for every vertex. Strict hub and minimum-rank domination are elementary factor inequalities; the epsilon-construction with a strictly positive logarithmic derivative proves all other ranks attainable. The actual package verify.py returned VERIFY_OK on 247 rational Krylov determinant instances and 36 rank constructions; the finite tests are not used as infinite proofs.

value.rationale: Single-node diffusion observation is a natural system-identification and network design question, and D-optimal volume is an established quality measure (Summers--Lygeros 2013, Fitch--Leonard 2016). The theorem removes all eigenvalue and Gramian calculations from exact placement on weighted stars, proves that a hub and the minimum-conductance leaf are dominated, and completely specifies observable sensors at repeated-conductance singularities. The constructive theorem demonstrates that every other edge-weight rank is genuinely feasible as a unique optimum, so simple highest-degree or always-largest-weight rules fail. This is a natural exact all-parameter classification, not an arbitrary finite parameter slice.
